chem-electro-001.title: Electrolysis: Mass Deposited at Cathode
chem-electro-001.body: During the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution using copper electrodes, a current of 2 A flows for 30 minutes. Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode. (Faraday constant F = 96500 C/mol, Relative atomic mass of Cu = 64)

chem-electro-001a.stepBody: Calculate the total charge (Q) using Q = It. Convert time to seconds first.
chem-electro-001a.stepExplanation: Q = It = 2 × (30 × 60) = 2 × 1800 = 3600 C (Convert minutes to seconds: 30 min = 1800 s)

chem-electro-001b.stepBody: Cu²⁺ requires 2 electrons per atom. Calculate moles of electrons, then moles and mass of Cu.
chem-electro-001b.stepExplanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Moles of electrons = Q/F = 3600/96500 = 0.0373 mol. Moles of Cu = 0.0373/2 = 0.0186 mol. Mass = nM = 0.0186 × 64 = 1.19 g

chem-electro-002.title: Electrolysis: Time Required
chem-electro-002.body: How long must a current of 3 A flow through molten sodium chloride to deposit 2.3 g of sodium at the cathode? (Faraday constant F = 96500 C/mol, Relative atomic mass of Na = 23)

chem-electro-002a.stepBody: Calculate the moles of sodium to be deposited using n = m/M.

chem-electro-002b.stepBody: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na. Calculate charge needed, then time using t = Q/I.
chem-electro-002b.stepExplanation: Charge Q = nF = 0.1 × 96500 = 9650 C. Time t = Q/I = 9650/3 = 3217 s = 53.6 minutes
